requirements.evidence: Contract implemented in routes/web.php:19-42 (guest login/register, POST logout, auth+verified home, password.request/email/reset/update, auth+signed+throttled verification routes), app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:40-81, app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:45-85, app/Http/Controllers/ForgotPasswordController.php:23-31, ResetPasswordController.php:28-57, LogoutController.php:15-23 and Auth/EmailVerificationController.php:13-43. Edge cases are tested: LoginTest.php:34-48 (session regeneration), 50-59 (intended URL), 75-88 (auth.failed), 105-128 (email+IP throttle); RegisterTest.php:49-66 (unverified/hashed/VerifyEmail/session), 68-77 (Registered), 76-84 (lowercase unique), 86-94 (confirmed), 96-102 (Password::defaults), 122-134 (IP throttle); PasswordResetTest.php:74-90 (remember_token rotation/PasswordReset); EmailVerificationTest.php:52-79 (tampered id/hash/unsigned link => 403); HomeAccessTest.php:12-25 (auth+verified); LocalizationTest.php:21-60 (pt_BR/en).

conventions.evidence: Uses the project patterns well: anonymous Blade components resources/views/components/{card,field,layouts/app}.blade.php, Bulma classes, route() for every link/action (resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:5, resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php:21-36), User::EMAIL_RULES shared from app/Models/User.php:25, Fillable/Hidden attributes (User.php:13-14), named-route redirects in Livewire (Login.php:69, Register.php:78), docs and changelog kept in sync (CHANGELOG.md:15-20, docs/business-rules.md:58-71). Deviations: validation is declared via a protected rules() method at Login.php:28 and Register.php:31 instead of the stated #[Validate] pattern (conventions.md:36), and ForgotPasswordController.php:29, ResetPasswordController.php:55 and EmailVerificationController.php:41 use back() rather than named routes.

security.evidence: Server-side validation on every action: Login.php:28-35/40-42 and Register.php:31-38/45-63; rate limits inside the Livewire actions (Login.php:46-63, Register.php:47-63) and on HTTP routes (routes/web.php:29-31, 37-42); strict e-mail rule at User.php:25; mass-assignment protected by #[Fillable] and #[Hidden] (User.php:13-14); passwords hashed via the model cast (RegisterTest.php:49-65); all views escape with {{ }} (resources/views/components/field.blade.php:2-14, layouts/app.blade.php:8-32); POST forms carry @csrf (resources/views/auth/verify-email.blade.php:5-6, layouts/app.blade.php:27-28); logout invalidates the session and rotates CSRF (LogoutController.php:15-20); reset rotates remember_token (ResetPasswordController.php:39-45); verification is auth+signed (routes/web.php:35-39).

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage for every feature: tests/Feature/Auth/LoginTest.php:1-153, RegisterTest.php:1-148, PasswordResetTest.php:1-132, EmailVerificationTest.php:1-133, HomeAccessTest.php:1-38, LogoutTest.php:1-39, LocalizationTest.php:1-65 and ViewConventionsTest.php:1-32. Failure paths are covered (wrong credentials, strict e-mail, confirmation/default password, invalid/unknown token, tampered id/hash, unsigned link, all throttles, guests, verified resend) and no existing tests were weakened. Missing: a direct Livewire unauthorized-call test for the guest-only Login::submit/Register::submit actions (only the route-level redirect is tested at LoginTest.php:28-32 and RegisterTest.php:43-47), which the project's Livewire definition of done asks for.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel primitives (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, Password::defaults, RateLimiter, Route::livewire) instead of a starter kit; small anonymous components (resources/views/components/card.blade.php:1-9, field.blade.php:1-16); shared e-mail rules in one constant (app/Models/User.php:25); no service/repository layer, no speculative abstraction and no duplicated controllers.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods (Login::submit at Login.php:40-70, Register::submit at Register.php:45-79), named constants (Login.php:17, Register.php:18), clear controller actions (ForgotPasswordController.php:23-31, ResetPasswordController.php:28-57, EmailVerificationController.php:13-43) and descriptive tests; no dead code, debug output or inconsistent style.

scope.evidence: Only auth-related app code, lang files, layout/components, route/provider wiring, docs and tests are added; phpunit.xml:22-23 only pins APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE, .env.example:1-8 only carries the required APP_NAME/APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE values, and there are no SCSS/JS, nginx/Docker, mail-theme or unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: Validation is declared with a protected rules() method instead of the project's stated #[Validate] attribute plus $this->validate() pattern (conventions.md:36); Livewire's security policy permits rules(), so this is a style deviation rather than a defect.

These handlers use back() instead of a named route, while the task's convention says controllers and Livewire auth classes redirect with named routes; back() is idiomatic for form errors and the resend flow, so this is only a nit.

The guest-only rule is tested only at the route level; there is no direct Livewire unauthorized-call test showing that an authenticated user invoking Login::submit/Register::submit is denied, which the project's Livewire definition of done asks for.

review.summary: The change adds the full in-app session-auth stack (Livewire login/register, logout, home, forgot/reset password and e-mail verification) in pt-BR with English fallback, plus layouts, shared components, translations, docs and extensive tests. It meets the functional contract and the security-sensitive parts (hashing, rate limits, signed verification, token rotation, escaping) are solid; the findings are minor convention/test-coverage nits (rules() instead of #[Validate], back()-style redirects, and no direct Livewire unauthorized-call test for the guest actions).
